content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.MIAMI – A sixth champion will be crowned today as the United States battles Venezuela in the World Baseball Classic title game Tuesday, March 17 at loanDepot Park in Miami, Florida. This game is available to watch on multiple streaming services.How do I watch Team USA vs. Venezuela for free? The game will broadcast live on FOX with the first pitch at 8 p.m. Eastern. Those who have cut the cable cord – or those who are blacked out by ongoing DIRECTV carriage dispute – can catch the game for free by utilizing streaming alternatives like FuboTV, which is offering a free trial and $25 off your first month. The most flexible option is SlingTV, which now offers new users a Day Pass for $4.99, Weekend Pass for $9.99, Week Pass for $14.99, Monthly for $45.99 and Season Pass for $199.99 for five months and $45.99 per month thereafter. All columns visible (no scrolling needed)Team USAThe United States (5-1) is coming off a thrilling 2-1 victory over the Dominican Republic in the semifinals. The American pitching staff put forth a gem to hold off the historic firepower of the DR, punching their third consecutive trip to the WBC finale.With only one game left to play in the tournament, the Americans’ high-powered offense might not ever reach its potential. They have scored 3, 6, 5 and 2 runs in their last four games. The Americans are once again turning to New York Mets MLB newcomer Nolan McLean after he was shell-shocked against Italy. He allowed three earned runs in three innings, including two home runs. David Bednar and Mason Miller anchor the bullpen for the Stars and Stripes.Team USA is playing on one day rest, while Venezuela will be playing off abundant emotion from their come-from-behind victory over the Italians. The United States’ lone championship came in 2017. Watch USA vs. Venezuela for free on FuboTVVenezuelaDays after stunning Shohei Ohtani and defending champion Japan, Venezuela (5-1) used a three-run seventh inning to topple undefeated Italy, 4-2, in the semifinals on March 16. The Venezuelans are playing for their first-ever WBC championship. Though they trail the Americans in OPS, batting average, RBI, runs scored, hits and slugging percentage, Venezuela ties the United States with nine home runs, which is fourth in the tournament. If this becomes a firework fest, it will force the American bats to come to life or face defeat. Venezuela’s hopes lie in veteran lefthander Eduardo Rodriguez, who allowed three earned runs and two home runs in two and a third innings of work. The Venezuelans also boast a potent bullpen, if available. The United States leads the all-time series, 3-2. The Americans have outscored Venezuela, 37-30, in those five games.
